1.q: כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל
1.note: See how you translated **Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel** in 29:4.

Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of sorrow over the disaster that is coming to **Nebo**. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How sad it will be for Nebo]
The word **Nebo** is the name of a town.

The expression **she is devastated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was the invading army. Alternate translation: [the invading army has devastated her]

Yahweh is speaking of **Kiriathaim** as if it were a living thing that could feel shame. He means that the people of Kiriathaim are ashamed because enemies have captured their town. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people of Kiriathaim are ashamed; enemies have captured their town]
The word **Kiriathaim** is the name of a town.

The expression **she is captured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was the invading army. Alternate translation: [the invading army has captured her]

Here, **The stronghold** represents “the people who defend the stronghold.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The people who defend the stronghold are put to shame and are dismayed]

The expression **is put to shame** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was the invading army. Alternate translation: [The stronghold has suffered shame]
See how you translated this name in 20:12.

2.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **praise** that is related to **Moab**. This could mean: (1) the praise that other people give to Moab or (2) the fame that Moab boasts about. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [praise that people give to Moab]

The pronoun **they** refers to the enemies of Moab, and the pronoun **her** refers to Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [In Heshbon the enemies of Moab have devised evil against Moab]
This is poetic language. In the original language, the name **Heshbon** sounds like the word translated **devised**. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here.

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Their plan is to come and cut her off from being a nation]

Here the enemies of Moab are speaking as if they could **cut her off** the way someone cuts a branch off a tree. They mean that they intend to destroy Moab completely so that it is no longer a nation. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and let us completely end her existence as a nation]
This is poetic language. In the original language, the name **Madmen** sounds like the word translated **be silenced**. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here.
The word **Madmen** is the name of a town.

The expression **you will be silenced** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it will be the enemy army. Alternate translation: [the enemy army will silence you]

Here, **the sword** represents “an attacking army.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [after you an attacking army will go]

3.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [A sound of a cry is heard from Horonaim]
The word **Horonaim** is the name of a town.

The terms **destruction** and **great breaking** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [complete destruction]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:6.

4.note: The expression **Moab is broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has broken Moab]

Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Moab is completely defeated]

The implication is that people in Moab are crying out loudly in distress. This could mean: (1) **her little ones** are the young children of Moab or (2) **her little ones** are the smaller towns of Moab, whose people are crying out. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [her young children are crying out loudly in distress so that people hear them]
The pronoun **her** refers to Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the little ones of Moab]
See how you translated the similar expression in 18:22.

5.note: The word **Luhith** is the name of a town.

The pronoun **he** refers to the people of Moab who are fleeing from their enemies. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [with weeping the people of Moab go up weeping]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the word **weeping** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [he goes up weeping bitterly]

The implication is that the people of Moab are crying out because their towns are being destroyed. This could mean: (1) **the adversaries** of Moab have heard this cry or (2) people have heard distressing cries, if the word translated **adversaries** means “distresses” here. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the adversaries of Moab have heard the people crying out because their towns are being destroyed]
See how you translated this name in 48:3.

6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a juniper bush in the wilderness** is alone and has very little to sustain it, so the people of Moab who flee will be alone and in great need. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and you will be alone in the wilderness with very little to keep you alive]
The word **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [so that you will be]

7.note: The word **your** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Moab as if it were a woman, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that the people of Moab relied on these things to keep them safe. This could mean: (1) **your works** are the things that Moab had achieved or (2) **your works** are the idols that the people of Moab had made. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your trusting in your achievements and in your treasures to keep you safe]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **trusting**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how you trust]

The expression **you also will be captured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it will be the enemy army. Alternate translation: [the enemy army will capture you also]

Here, **Chemosh** represents “the idol of Chemosh.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And the idol of Chemosh will go out into exile]
The word **Chemosh** is the name of a false god that the people of Moab worshiped.

8.note: Yahweh is speaking of each **city** as if it were a living thing that could **escape**. He means that the people of every city will be unable to escape. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and no one in any city will escape]

Yahweh is referring to all of Moab by naming two major components, **the valley** and **the plateau**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And the whole land of Moab will be destroyed]

The expression **the plateau will be destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it will be Yahweh. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh will destroy the plateau]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [as I, Yahweh, have said]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:15.

9.q: תְּנוּ צִ֣יץ לְ⁠מוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י נָצֹ֖א תֵּצֵ֑א
9.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if Moab were a bird that could fly away if someone gave it a **wing**. It means that the people of Moab will need to flee very quickly from their enemies. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Enable Moab to flee swiftly, for she will hurry away in haste]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **desolation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and her cities will become completely deserted]

10.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific person by **the one doing the work of Yahweh**. He means people in general who are supposed to do this work. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [anyone who does the work of Yahweh]

The implication is that **the work of Yahweh** is the work of destroying Moab, which Yahweh has given the enemy army to do. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s work of destroying Moab]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **slackness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [lazily]

10.q: אָר֗וּר עֹשֶׂ֛ה מְלֶ֥אכֶת יְהוָ֖ה רְמִיָּ֑ה וְ⁠אָר֕וּר מֹנֵ֥עַ חַרְבּ֖⁠וֹ מִ⁠דָּֽם

If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Cursed is anyone who does not fully carry out Yahweh’s work of killing with the sword]

10.q: אָר֗וּר עֹשֶׂ֛ה מְלֶ֥אכֶת יְהוָ֖ה רְמִיָּ֑ה וְ⁠אָר֕וּר מֹנֵ֥עַ חַרְבּ֖⁠וֹ מִ⁠דָּֽם

11.q: וְ⁠שֹׁקֵ֥ט הוּא֙ אֶל־שְׁמָרָ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠לֹֽא־הוּרַ֤ק מִ⁠כְּלִי֙ אֶל־כֶּ֔לִי & עָמַ֤ד טַעְמ⁠וֹ֙ בּ֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠רֵיח֖⁠וֹ לֹ֥א נָמָֽר & וְ⁠שִׁלַּחְתִּי־ל֥⁠וֹ צֹעִ֖ים וְ⁠צֵעֻ֑⁠הוּ וְ⁠כֵלָ֣י⁠ו יָרִ֔יקוּ וְ⁠נִבְלֵי⁠הֶ֖ם יְנַפֵּֽצוּ
11.note: Yahweh draws an extended comparison between the people Moab and grape juice that is in the process of being turned into fully matured wine. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the comparison as in the UST.

If you must state who did the action, you could use a general expression such as “no one.” Alternate translation: [And no one has emptied him from vessel to vessel]

11.q: שַׁאֲנַ֨ן מוֹאָ֜ב מִ⁠נְּעוּרָ֗י⁠ו וְ⁠שֹׁקֵ֥ט הוּא֙ אֶל־שְׁמָרָ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠לֹֽא־הוּרַ֤ק מִ⁠כְּלִי֙ & כֶּ֔לִי וּ⁠בַ⁠גּוֹלָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָלָ֑ךְ
11.note: Hebrew poetry sometimes uses a literary device called a “chiasm” (sometimes called “chiasmus”). A chiasm is when words or phrases are ordered in an A-B-B-A sequence. Here the information is presented like this: A) a literal statement: “Moab has been at ease from his youth” B) a metaphorical statement: Moab “is undisturbed on his dregs” B) a metaphorical statement: Moab “has not been emptied from vessel to vessel” A) a literal statement: Moab will go “into exile.” If possible, try to follow this A-B-B-A sequence of presenting the information here.

In this verse, the word **Moab** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of Moab as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form, such as “the people of Moab.” Alternate translation: [The people of Moab have been at ease from their youth]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:6.

12.q: And they will empty his vessels and they will shatter their jars
12.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the enemies of the Moabites both times it is used here, while the pronouns **his** and **their** both refer to the Moabites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the enemies of the Moabites will empty the Moabites’ vessels and those enemies will shatter the Moabites’ jars]

Alternate translation: [to him tippers, and they will tip him. And they will empty his vessels and they will shatter his jars]

Yahweh is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [pay attention]

If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [when Chemosh cannot save them, just as the house of Israel was ashamed when the idol at Bethel that they relied on could not save them]

14.q: אֵ֚יךְ תֹּֽאמְר֔וּ גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְ⁠אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֖יִל לַ⁠מִּלְחָמָֽה
14.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the people of Moab cannot rightly claim to be strong warriors. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You cannot rightly say, ‘We are mighty, and men of valor for battle’!]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [say that you are mighty men of valor for battle]

The terms **mighty** and **men of valor** mean similar things. The people of Moab are using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [We are very brave warriors]

The people of Moab are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and we are men of valor who are ready for battle]

Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the enemy has killed the choicest of his young men]

21.note: Yahweh is speaking of **judgment** as if it were a living thing that could come to a place. He means that he has punished the people who live on the plateau. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I have brought punishment to the land of the plateau]

21.q: אֶל חֹל֥וֹן וְ⁠אֶל יַ֖הְצָ⁠ה וְ⁠עַל מופעת
21.note: The words **Holon**, **Jahaz**, and **Mephaath** are the names of towns.

21.q: אֶל חֹל֥וֹן וְ⁠אֶל יַ֖הְצָ⁠ה וְ⁠עַל מופעת
21.note: Yahweh uses a repetitive series of clauses from here through verse 24 to communicate that what he is saying should be understood as comprehensive and overwhelming. Use a form in your language that someone would use to describe a situation that is comprehensive and overwhelming.

22.q: וְ⁠עַל דִּיב֣וֹן וְ⁠עַל נְב֔וֹ וְ⁠עַל בֵּ֖ית דִּבְלָתָֽיִם
22.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and judgment has come upon Dibon and upon Nebo and upon Beth Diblathaim]
The words **Beth Diblathaim** are the name of a town.
See how you translated this name in [48:1](ta:48).

23.note: The words **Beth Gamul** and **Beth Meon** are the names of towns.
See how you translated this name in [48:1](ta:48).

24.note: The words **Kerioth** and **Bozrah** are the names of towns.

Yahweh is using the adjectives **far** and **near** as nouns to mean certain kinds of cities. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [the cities that are far away and the cities that are near]

Yahweh is referring to all of the cities of Moab by naming two extremes, **the far** and **the near**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [every one of them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:15.

25.note: The expressions **has been cut off** and **has been broken** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has cut off the horn of Moab, and he has broken his arm]
See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of clauses in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [Moab’s strength has been completely destroyed]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Moab were an animal whose **horn** has **been cut off**. It means that Moab has lost its strength. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Moab has lost his strength]
Here, **arm** represents “power.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and his power has been destroyed]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.

26.note: The pronoun **him** refers to Moab. Yahweh does not say whom he is commanding, but it is probably the enemies whom he is sending against Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Enemies of Moab, make Moab drunk]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his punishment were a strong drink that would make Moab **drunk**. It means that Yahweh will punish Moab so severely that its people will be helpless and disgraced, like a drunk person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Punish him so severely that he becomes helpless]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [because against me he has made himself great]

Yahweh is using **made himself great** as a common expression of the culture to mean “proudly defied.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he has proudly defied Yahweh]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Moab were a drunk person who falls and rolls around **in his vomit**. It means that Moab will be completely humiliated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Moab will be completely humiliated]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **derision**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he also will be someone whom people mock]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:7.

27.q: וְ⁠אִ֣ם ל֣וֹא הַ⁠שְּׂחֹ֗ק הָיָ֤ה לְ⁠ךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
27.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the people of Moab mocked the people of Israel. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For Israel certainly came to be a derision to you!]

27.q: וְ⁠אִ֣ם ל֣וֹא הַ⁠שְּׂחֹ֗ק הָיָ֤ה לְ⁠ךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
27.note: In this verse, the word **Israel** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of Israel as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form, such as “the people of Israel.” Alternate translation: [For did not the people of Israel come to be a derision to you]

27.q: אִם בְּ⁠גַנָּבִ֖ים נמצאה כִּֽי מִ⁠דֵּ֧י דְבָרֶ֥י⁠ךָ בּ֖⁠וֹ תִּתְנוֹדָֽד
27.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that Israel had done nothing to deserve such mocking from Moab. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [He was not found among thieves, yet as often as your words were about him you shook your head at him!]

The expression **Was he found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could use a general expression such as “people.” Alternate translation: [Did people find him among thieves]
The words **your** and **you** are singular here because Yahweh is addressing Moab as if it were a man, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Shaking the head was a symbolic action by which the people of Moab showed that they despised the people of Israel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [you shook your head in contempt of him]

28.note: The implication is that the people of Moab should take refuge in the caves and cliffs of the rocky hills. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and take refuge among the rocky cliffs of the hills]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a dove** builds its nest in hidden places on cliffs where enemies cannot reach it, so the people of Moab should hide in places that are hard to reach. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and hide where enemies cannot reach you, just as a dove nests]

Yahweh is using **the mouth of a pit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the opening of a ravine.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the opening of a ravine]

29.note: The pronoun **We** could refer to: (1) Yahweh and his heavenly council or (2) Jeremiah and the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, and my heavenly council have heard of]

The terms **loftiness**, **pride**, **arrogance**, and **the height of his heart** mean similar things. Yahweh is using these terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [how extremely arrogant he is]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Moab’s **heart** had great **height**. It means that the people of Moab think that they are better than other people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the way he thinks he is superior to others]

30.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the declaration of Yahweh** before the information about what Yahweh knows. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, declare that I know his outburst]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **outburst**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how he rages]

The implication is that Yahweh knows about the proud and angry words of Moab. This could mean: (1) **outburst** refers to the insolent boasting of Moab or (2) **outburst** refers to the fury of Moab. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [his arrogant, angry words]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.
See how you translated the similar expression in 36:18.

31.q: עַל כֵּן֙ עַל מוֹאָ֣ב אֲיֵלִ֔יל וּ⁠לְ⁠מוֹאָ֥ב כֻּלֹּ֖⁠ה אֶזְעָ֑ק אֶל אַנְשֵׁ֥י קִֽיר חֶ֖רֶשׂ יֶהְגֶּֽה
31.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of clauses in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [Therefore I will mourn deeply for all the people of Moab, including the men of Kir Hareseth]

The pronoun **he** could refer to: (1) Yahweh, who is speaking about himself or (2) anyone in general who moans for these men. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for the men of Kir Hareseth I, Yahweh, will moan]
The words **Kir Hareseth** are the name of a city.

Most ancient manuscripts read “he will moan.” The ULT follows that reading. One ancient manuscript and the Eastern Qere (scribal correction) read “I will moan.” The UST follows that reading. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the UST.
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:6.

32.note: Yahweh is speaking to the **vine of Sibmah** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the destruction of Moab. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the vine of Sibmah. Alternate translation: [I will weep for the vine of Sibmah]

32.q: מִ⁠בְּכִ֨י יַעְזֵ֤ר אֶבְכֶּה לָּ⁠ךְ֙ הַ⁠גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה
32.note: The words **Jazer** and **Sibmah** are the names of towns.

32.q: עַל קֵיצֵ֥⁠ךְ וְ⁠עַל בְּצִירֵ֖⁠ךְ שֹׁדֵ֥ד נָפָֽל
32.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the vine of Sibmah had **summer fruit** and a **grape harvest** on which **a destroyer has fallen**. It means that the enemy has destroyed the crops and the prosperity of Moab. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [An enemy has destroyed your crops and all your prosperity]

This could mean: (1) Yahweh weeps over the destruction of the people of Sibmah more than he weeps over the people of Jazer. Alternate translation: [More than I weep over the people of Jazer] (2) Yahweh weeps over the destruction of the people of Sibmah more than the people of Jazer weep over the destruction of the people of Sibmah. Alternate translation: [More than the people of Jazer weep]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Sibmah and its people were a **vine**. It means that Sibmah was a prosperous town that was famous for its vineyards. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Sibmah, town famous for your vineyards]

32.q: נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֨יִ⁠ךְ֙ עָ֣בְרוּ יָ֔ם עַ֛ד יָ֥ם יַעְזֵ֖ר נָגָ֑עוּ
32.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the vineyards of Moab were a vine whose **tendrils** spread a great distance. It means that the vineyards and prosperity of Moab extended over a large area. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Your vineyards and prosperity spread out as far as the sea; they extended all the way to the sea of Jazer]

33.note: The expression **have been taken away** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was Yahweh. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh has taken away gladness and rejoicing]

The terms **gladness** and **rejoicing** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [all joyful celebrations]

The implication is that because Yahweh has destroyed the vineyards, there is no longer any grape harvest, so people no longer make wine and celebrate. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And I have destroyed the vineyards, so there are no grapes to make wine in the winepresses]

33.q: לֹֽא יִדְרֹ֣ךְ הֵידָ֔ד הֵידָ֖ד לֹ֥א הֵידָֽד
33.note: The implication is that the joyful shouting of the people who tread grapes will end. The second part of this sentence could mean: (1) there will be no harvest shout at all or (2) the shouting that people hear will be the battle cry of enemies, not the joyful shout of people harvesting grapes. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [No one will shout for joy while treading the grapes; there will be no harvest shout at all]

The pronoun **He** refers to anyone who treads grapes in the winepresses to make wine. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [No one who treads the grapes will tread with a shout]

34.q: מִ⁠זַּעֲקַ֨ת חֶשְׁבּ֜וֹן עַד אֶלְעָלֵ֗ה עַד יַ֨הַץ֙ נָתְנ֣וּ קוֹלָ֔⁠ם
34.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the people who **have given their voice** before the information about the places from which they cried out. Alternate translation: [They have given their voice from the outcry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz]
The words **Elealeh** and **Jahaz** are the names of towns.
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:15.

This could mean: (1) **Eglath Shelishiyah** is the name of another town or (2) it is a title meaning “a third heifer” that describes the town of Horonaim. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the town of Eglath Shelishiyah]
See how you translated this name in 48:3.

35.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific person who offers sacrifices or who is **burning incense**. He means anyone in Moab who does these things. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those who cause offerings to ascend on high places and those who burn incense to their gods]

The implication is that **a high place** was a hilltop where people worshiped false gods and offered sacrifices to them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on a hilltop shrine for worshiping false gods]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.

36.q: עַל כֵּ֞ן לִבִּ֤⁠י לְ⁠מוֹאָב֙ כַּ⁠חֲלִלִ֣ים יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְ⁠לִבִּ⁠י֙ אֶל אַנְשֵׁ֣י קִֽיר חֶ֔רֶשׂ כַּ⁠חֲלִילִ֖ים יֶהֱמֶ֑ה
36.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of clauses in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [Therefore my heart moans like flutes for Moab and for the men of Kir Hareseth]

The point of this comparison is that just as **flutes** make a mournful sound at funerals, so Yahweh’s **heart moans** with grief for Moab. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [my heart grieves for Moab with a sad sound, the way flutes wail at a funeral]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **heart** could moan like a person. It means that he feels deep sorrow. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I wail in deep sorrow]
The pronoun **he** refers to the people of Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the abundance the people of Moab have acquired has perished]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abundance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [everything that he has plentifully acquired]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:6.

37.q: כָל רֹאשׁ֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְ⁠כָל זָקָ֖ן גְּרֻעָ֑ה
37.note: Shaving the head and clipping the beard were symbolic actions by which people showed that they were mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of these actions in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [every head will be shaved bald, and every beard will be clipped to show that they are mourning]

The expression **will be clipped** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it will be the mourners themselves. Alternate translation: [and every man will clip his beard]

37.q: עַ֤ל כָּל יָדַ֨יִם֙ גְּדֻדֹ֔ת וְ⁠עַל מָתְנַ֖יִם שָֽׂק
37.note: Cutting the hands and wearing sackcloth were symbolic actions by which people showed that they were mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of these actions in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [On all hands will be gashes, and on the loins will be sackcloth to show that they are mourning]

38.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the places in Moab by naming two major components, **the housetops** and **her open squares**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [In every place in Moab, both private and public]

Yahweh says **all of it lamentation** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [there is much lamentation everywhere]

38.q: שָׁבַ֣רְתִּי אֶת מוֹאָ֗ב כִּ⁠כְלִ֛י אֵֽין חֵ֥פֶץ בּ֖⁠וֹ
38.note: The point of this comparison is that just as someone breaks and throws away **a vessel without delight in it**, so Yahweh has destroyed Moab because it has no value to him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [I have destroyed Moab because it has no value to me, just as someone breaks and throws away a worthless jar]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.

39.note: The pronoun **it** refers to Moab, and the pronoun **They** refers to the people of Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [How Moab is dismayed! The people of Moab wail]

Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of sorrow. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Alas, it is terribly dismayed]

Yahweh is using the expression about turning the **neck** as a common expression of the culture to mean “turned back and fled.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [How Moab has turned back and fled in shame]

39.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֥ה מוֹאָ֛ב לִ⁠שְׂחֹ֥ק וְ⁠לִ⁠מְחִתָּ֖ה לְ⁠כָל סְבִיבָֽי⁠ו
39.note: If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **derision** and **terror**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Moab has become something that people mock and something that frightens all around him]

40.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention]

The pronoun **he** could refer to: (1) the king of the enemy army or (2) Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [like an eagle the enemy king will swoop down]

The point of this comparison is that just as **an eagle** swoops down quickly to catch its prey, so the enemy will attack Moab quickly and powerfully. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [he will attack quickly and powerfully, like an eagle swooping down on its prey]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the enemy were an eagle that will **spread his wings** over Moab. It means that the enemy army will cover the land of Moab and conquer it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will cover the land of Moab with his army and conquer it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5.

41.note: The expressions **has been captured** and **have been seized** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was the enemy army. Alternate translation: [The enemy army has captured Kerioth, and it has seized the strongholds]

41.q: וְֽ֠⁠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ בַּ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠ה֔וּא כְּ⁠לֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה
41.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a woman in labor** is in great pain and distress, so the warriors of Moab will be in great fear and distress. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And in that day the warriors of Moab will be in great fear and distress, just as a woman in labor is in great pain]

In this verse, the word **heart** is singular in form, but it refers to the hearts of all the warriors of Moab as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “heart.” Alternate translation: [the hearts of the warriors of Moab]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:9.

42.note: The expression **Moab will be destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who will do the action, it will be Yahweh. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will destroy Moab so that it is no longer a people]
See how you translated the similar expression in 48:26.

43.note: This is poetic language. In the original language, the words translated **Terror**, **pit**, and **snare** sound very similar. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Moab were animals that hunters catch in a **pit** or a **snare**. It means that the people of Moab will not be able to escape from destruction. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and destruction that you cannot escape]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.

44.q: ה⁠ניס מִ⁠פְּנֵ֤י הַ⁠פַּ֨חַד֙ יִפֹּ֣ל אֶל הַ⁠פַּ֔חַת וְ⁠הָֽ⁠עֹלֶה֙ מִן הַ⁠פַּ֔חַת יִלָּכֵ֖ד בַּ⁠פָּ֑ח
44.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Moab were animals trying to escape from hunters who have set traps such as **the pit** and **the snare**. It means that whatever the people of Moab do to escape, they will still be destroyed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The one fleeing from the terror will not escape, and the one who escapes that disaster will be destroyed by another]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific person by **The one fleeing**. He means anyone who flees. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone who flees from the face of the terror]

Yahweh is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “away from.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [away from the terror]

The expression **will be caught** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state what will do the action, you could say that the snare will catch him. Alternate translation: [will step into the snare that will catch him]

44.q: אָבִ֨יא אֵלֶ֧י⁠הָ אֶל מוֹאָ֛ב שְׁנַ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖⁠ם
44.note: The pronoun **her** refers to Moab, and the pronoun **their** refers to the people of Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I will bring to the land of Moab the year of the visitation of the people of Moab]
See how you translated this phrase in 11:23.
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.

45.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the city of Heshbon cast a **shadow** in which people could find shelter. It means that the people who are fleeing hope to find protection in Heshbon.
